Arteta with a double sub: Gyokeres and Merino on for Havertz and Rice, which comes as something of a surprise.

In a recent development, hull’s goalkeeper Tzolakis has just saved with his feet to deny Madueke. A few minutes earlier, Konsa blocked a Cho shot after a threatening Hull break. Still no opening goal.

According to recent reports, it has been all Newcastle at the start of the second half and Harvey Barnes has now failed to take a hat-trick of chances. This was the best of the lot, running on to the ball, middle of the area from a perfectly weighted Yoane Wissa pass, he blasted a shot the wrong side of the post.

The second halves at the Emirates and Craven Cottage have kicked off. No changes from Arsenal, Hull, Fulham or Newcastle.

While Kai Havertz was in an offside position when his shirt was pulled, he may not have been active.

The law states: “A player in an offside position is moving towards the ball with the intention of playing the ball and is fouled before playing or attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball, the foul is penalised as it has occurred before the offside offence.”.

However, the Premier League match centre does not see it that way.

Hopefully there will be more action in the second 45 minutes at Craven Cottage and the Emirates.

In a recent development, an odd moment at the Emirates. Referee Farai Hallam was sent to monitor to look at a shirt pull on Kai Havertz in the Hull box. Through his headset, he tells the crowd that a “holding offence” has been committed – cue cheers from the Arsenal fans – before adding “however, the Arsenal player was in an offside position”. So no penalty. It would have been very soft in any case, Havertz was not close to reaching the rebound from a long shot.

Mikel Arteta predictably furious to not get a penalty, even though Havertz was clearly offside before being pulled.

It has been revealed that I’ve spotted something else since I was covering Arsenal in 2018. I was gazing up at the boards that circle the top tier where the club mark every trophy that the team has won. There was previously this major gap, of course, from 2005 until 2014 before the cabinet gradually began refilling. But someone has since had a good idea. They have added all the women’s trophies as well, transforming the tally by just the odd 17 during those tricky years of transition and billionaire rivals owners in the men’s game.

Declan Rice has also just had a shot flash wide, but still no clear chances for either team.

Dan Burn thought he had scored from close-range, but Wissa has been penalised for blocking Castagne so the goal was ruled out.

Sources indicate that some controversy here as Newcastle appear to have had a perfectly good goal ruled out for an innocuous looking foul from Yoane Wissa on Timothy Costagne inside the box. Dan Burn was the scorer. Newcastle’s bench are furious. Most of us are just bemused.

Sources indicate that arsenal have largely been on top after Hull’s lively start but clear chances are scarce and Hull’s fans certainly sound increasingly confident. “You’re only here for the Tigers”, they say. To which a rendition of “champions” rings out. On that note, they had a replica of the Premier League trophy outside the Emirates before the match, with fans queuing up to get their photo with it.

Recent findings suggest that it’s always great to be back home. It’s the last game before the international break so we know the importance of that and the challenges Hull will provide today. We’re super focused, it’s a massive game for us.

Industry observers note that with the amount of games we’re playing, we need that freshness. The team has been performing really well, the finishers have been key again and that’s what we have today – start the game really, really strong and if we need to, have the ability to change the game.

Mikel Arteta has said Arsenal are “looking after” Declan Rice more now than in any previous campaign and has rejected suggestions that the England midfielder is being overplayed.

Rice played through nerve pain in his hamstring in the second half of last season, when he made an extraordinary 69 appearances for club and country.

The 27-year-old has played at least 60 matches in each of the past four campaigns, prompting concerns among Arsenal supporters that he is at risk of burnout or injury.

Arteta kept Rice on the field for the full 90 minutes of Arsenal’s midweek victory over Slavia Prague but insisted the club is working harder than ever to manage the midfielder’s workload.

So far this season, Rice has been left out of Arsenal’s two Carabao Cup matches and also withdrew from the previous international break in September.

In a recent development, asked if he was concerned about Rice’s fitness, Arteta remarked: “Concerns? Which is the only player, the only player in this squad, that for two games in the Carabao Cup has been left out of the squad? At home with two days off? It’s not true [that Rice is being overplayed].

“We are really looking after him more than any other season. The way he is training and all the love [he is being shown]. That’s it.

“Here are the demands of this football club and a player like him. Not only him, because there are many others that have even less time. That’s it. That has to be the mindset. If you start to put other things in your brain, [it will create] damage. Erase them, get them in the bin and just focus on what you have to do.”.

Newly-promoted Hull City stunned Arsenal at the Emirates thanks to goals from Geovanni and Daniel Cousin in September 2008, but you will find long odds on them repeating the feat this afternoon.

With Manchester City playing at Nottingham Forest in the later kick-off, Mikel Arteta’s team have the chance to extend their lead at the top of the Premier League and make it 27 points from a possible 30 going into the international break.

Victory at Anfield last weekend was achieved with steel and resolve, but the more intricate side of Arsenal’s attacking play will be under the microscope against opponents likely to defend deep and in numbers.

With that in mind, it was noteworthy that Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard, Bruno Guimaraes and Myles Lewis-Skelly started the Champions League win at Slavia Prague on the bench, with only Odegaard coming on.

Declan Rice played the full 90 minutes, and one wonders if this is a rare chance for Arteta to leave him out of a Premier League starting XI.

According to recent reports, hull are 12th and have lost only two league games, a performance which far exceeds the gloomy pre-season forecasts for their chances. However, they are winless since the end of August and have not kept a clean sheet since a goalless draw with Aston Villa on Sept 4.

Newcastle were booed off at St James’ Park on Monday after their limp defeat by Everton, and have looked far too easy to play through all season, with their defensive statistics making for grim reading.

Alvaro Arbeloa was in Jaissle’s position a few weeks ago, but Fulham appear to have turned a corner and were impressive in a 1-1 at Villa Park last time out. John had watched the game on television, but was part of what must be a dwindling group who could say they were there the last time Wales had beaten Fresh Zealand, at the Arms Park in 1953.

#105704. NWSL, U.S. Soccer continue focus on women's soccer growth with player and executive development programs

NWSL, U.S. Soccer continue focus on women's soccer growth with player and executive development programs

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2000 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that WASHINGTON, D.C.
  • In the first of four announcements she teased was in service of that.
  • According to recent reports, the NWSL's newly introduced initiatives reflect a shifting focus across the American soccer landscape, one that seems driven by the heightened interest in the sport courtesy of this year's World Cup in North America.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that WASHINGTON, D.C. – The NWSL has always been a measuring stick for the growth of women's soccer in the U.S., which in recent years has been headlined by skyrocketing expansion fees and increased fan engagement. There's a buzzword that continues to pop up around the league, one that is rarely associated with the key performance indicators – pipeline. After she read out another list of attendance figures and viewership numbers before the 2026 season wraps up with Saturday's NWSL Championship (8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+), commissioner Jessica Berman made a hard pivot in her state of the league remarks on Thursday to say the league is officially in the business of prioritizing stated pipeline.

In the first of four announcements she teased was in service of that. The NWSL announced two initiatives on Thursday: the creation of a player development rule (PDR) and a sporting executive leadership program, designed specifically to focus on the foundation of the league's structure. The plans are a marriage of the league's business model and sporting objectives, a tacit understanding that the two go hand-in-hand, especially for a league that is admittedly driven by star power. These new plans, though, are hardly the only initiatives that will influence the pipeline.

According to recent reports, the NWSL's newly introduced initiatives reflect a shifting focus across the American soccer landscape, one that seems driven by the heightened interest in the sport courtesy of this year's World Cup in North America. The league's financial stability enabled this shift but beyond that, there are overlapping commitments across the industry to finally fix one of American soccer's most evident problems – the pipeline. The sport's success in this country has often come in spite of a fractured youth soccer system, one that U.S. Soccer hopes to unite in the coming years.

The parties, be it in conjunction or individually, are also dead set on ensuring the women's game is held in equal regard to the men's every step of the way.

The PDR joins a list of NWSL rules in recent years that have incentivized clubs to recruit young players more easily such as the U-18 Entry Mechanism and organizing its first-ever combine last year. The newly introduced rule requires participating clubs to develop a curriculum that supports player development and is tied directly to salary cap relief.

"What can we do at the league to motivate and incentivize clubs to develop players?" Sarah Gregorius, the NWSL's vice president of sporting, told CBS Sports. "What do we have in our toolkit? And one of the things we obviously have in our toolkit is a salary cap and we can use that as a motivation and as an incentive to encourage the types of behavior around player development that we want to see, and hopefully, it's really our first structural foray into player development. Again, it's deliberately an incentive. It's not a mandate. It's up to the clubs. If they want to participate, if they want to access the reward, they know what they have to do in order to do that.".

There is a perceived industry standard about developing young players, even if it is as far from an exact science as it gets. Academy systems tied to clubs are how players often come up the ranks – that is true across the men's game including in MLS and increasingly so for women's players in Europe. The NWSL does not have a streamlined system that mirrors the academy set-up and interestingly enough, is not actually trying to go in that direction.

According to recent reports, "This is a pretty unique country," Gregorius mentioned. "It doesn't actually work to pick something up from overseas and plop it down over here and I'm actually not convinced in the two years that I've spent here and everything that I've learned that this vertical academy system across the clubs makes the most sense. There's already a ton of incredible player development happening. There's just a bit of a lack of cohesion and a lack of connection to the professional game … The Spanish model won't work here, the German model wouldn't work here, the Japanese model wouldn't work here. Got a ton of respect for what they're doing in their countries but the reason that it works is it's for those countries. We have to do something that works for this one, which has characteristics that no other country in the world has. F---, this place is substantial. It's dynamic. There's a lot going on.".

Gregorius believes a league-issued mandate might further fracture an already splintered landscape.

"If I think about it from a local level, some of our clubs are in markets that have thriving youth ecosystems, right?" Gregorius started. "So if all of a sudden there was a mandate from the league that every single club – which is what they do in England – has to come in and have a professional game academy, they're going to all of a sudden have to start pulling players out of those environments, which is disruptive for the kids. It's disruptive for the families. Some of those kids and families are also fans of the team. It's the icing on the cake in those particular markets so all of a sudden, you create tension. You create tension for the parents. You create tension for the kids. You create tension within the fan groups. They're like, 'Well, no, actually. You've stripped out my youth club in order to service a mandate from the league, not paying attention to the fact that all of your talented players have come through the system.' That's not what we want. That's bad for player development and it's bad for fan engagement, to be honest.".

The NWSL is distinguishing itself from MLS, a league to which it has no formal ties but one that committed to the traditional academy system over a decade ago and can count it amongst its greatest successes. There's no stigma associated with the diverging path, though – U.S. Soccer has committed to viewing the women's game specifically through a female lens in recent years, an initiative championed by U.S. women's national team head coach Emma Hayes but embraced by many, either through her influence or separate from it.

"The intense focus on the pathway is very intentional," U.S. Soccer COO Dan Helfrich told CBS Sports. "The intense focus as we build the next version of the women and girls pathway, that it's done through a female lens, is very intentional and look, there is going to be, we believe, historic investment and interest in women's soccer and it's it's going to crescendo into the 2031 World Cup and making sure we take advantage of this moment to corral and direct the investment and interest in a sustainable way. I don't think there's anything that could have a greater legacy for women's soccer in our country than that.".

The distinction between the men's and women's games, even at the youth levels, is easy for Helfrich to make because they have always existed.

"The first thing is the environments for players to develop in," he noted. "it's really vital that they're tailored to women and girl  and that includes environments for youth clubs and colleges and professional clubs and so some of the work, for example, of the Kang Women's Institute becomes really important to do the research to develop the insights and then for us to promulgate them into all these areas, that's different and if you look at the as-is state of the pathway, the league structures for girls are different than the league structures for boys. The role of college soccer for girls is different than the role of college soccer for boys and so practically, if you're trying to optimize a future, you apply a different lens.".

There's more shared consensus when it comes to developing leaders that will foster players' growth, which is where the sporting executive leadership program kicks in. The program is built around specialized education for sporting director types, the first yearlong edition of the initiative already in session. A cohort of six – Haley Carter of the Washington Spirit, Caitlin Carducci of the Orlando Pride, Angela Mangano of the Houston Dash, Jeff Agoos of the Portland Thorns, Kelly Cousins of the Utah Royals and Dome Guasch of the Boston Legacy – already took part in their first session of a project supported both by U.S. Soccer and FIFA.

"The 16, now 18, individuals who hold the highest sporting position at the clubs have an outsized impact on the on-field identity and on-field product of their club so therefore, all of those people have an an impact on the on-field product of the league," Gregorius noted. "It's also, curiously enough, one of the few roles within the sporting department that doesn't have a license. You don't need to have completed a particular license. There's no education requirements or anything like that so when we also did an audit of the 16 clubs and who was holding those positions, some have former players, some have lawyers, some have people with an operations background, some have people with a coaching background. It was very varied so we're like, okay, if we know that this group has a ton of impact, if we know that they don't go through any structured learning. Is there a way that we can wrap our arms around them and support them?".

The uniqueness of this program is that it is tied specifically to the NWSL, which operates independently of a men's league unlike some of its European counterparts or even the WNBA.

"It's the first of its kind because every other f---ing part of the world just cares about men's football so we're really, really proud of not only the commitment and the discipline around trying to get it off the ground," Gregorius said.

It is in parallel with other initiatives the league and U.S. Soccer have worked on in recent years. The NWSL combine, for example, was also an effort to bolster female coaches while U.S. Soccer frequently uses its new national training center to conduct coaching courses with the youth game in mind.

Industry observers note that "What I would say is to grow the game the way it needs to be grown, we can't underestimate or overlook the non-player part of development," Helfrich noted, "and the non-player part of development is coaches. The non-player part of development is scouts. Non-player part of development is referees and the non-player part of development is front office, technical leaders and so, building a partnership with the NWSL on all of those important non-player development activities is a big priority.".

Industry observers note that the NWSL's partnership with U.S. Soccer on this program also speaks to a unique truth about American soccer. The women's game is held in incredibly high regard in the U.S. because of the historic success of the USWNT, who have four World Cup titles and five Olympic gold medals in their 40-year history. The USWNT's reputation of being serial winners is intrinsically tied to the health of the federation, the NWSL and in some ways, American soccer as a whole.

"Honest to God, I've loved waking up every day and only thinking about the women's game," Gregorius, a former Newly introduced Zealand international, said. "It's brilliant and it's very unique over here that we are able to do that and what I love about working with U.S. Soccer, as well, to be honest, is they're the same. They're almost more interested in the women's game sometimes than they are anything else … It's an organization that is already on the train, you know what I mean? The NWSL and our clubs, it's not even a question of being in the shadow of the men's game or any of that other bulls--- that you kind of encounter in other places. The focus is unwavering and that's brilliant.".

“I was doing a breakfast show on Radio London, but I had to go back to reading the news because I wasn't famous,” he continues.

After leaving the audition with low expectations, Rushden continued to explore other possibilities.

“In the meantime, I'd got an audition for Blue Peter,” he reveals before receiving a life-changing telephone call.

“Before I went to it, I got a call from Sky and they asked, “Do you want to do Soccer AM?” My head just exploded and I was trying to play it cool.

Latest Update: How a green economy could help reverse climate change

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1442 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Human civilization is currently profoundly unsustainable.
  • If economies and societies keep to business as usual, the Earth's vital processes will continue to be thrown wildly out of balance, threatening the future of humanity.
  • Recent findings suggest that it's now largely accepted that if humans are to have any chance of slowing global warming and nature loss, those social and economic models must change.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Human civilization is currently profoundly unsustainable. Earth has already crossed seven of the nine planetary boundaries critical for sustaining life, including climate change, ocean acidification and biosphere integrity.

If economies and societies keep to business as usual, the Earth's vital processes will continue to be thrown wildly out of balance, threatening the future of humanity.

Recent findings suggest that it's now largely accepted that if humans are to have any chance of slowing global warming and nature loss, those social and economic models must change. That's where the idea of green growth comes in.

Its promise is to keep growing the economy while reducing emissions and resource use. That involves, for instance, running factories, businesses and homes on wind, solar and other green energy instead of coal and gas, replacing gas-fired furnaces with heat pumps and  recycling and reusing resources and raw materials.

According to recent reports, "Basically, the idea is: business as usual, but with more sustainable technologies," remarked Helmut Haberl, a social ecology professor at BOKU University in Vienna. Along with his colleagues, he published a major report in 2020 evaluating more than 800 studies on green growth.

In principle, the world's economic output could continue to grow in the long term and generate significantly fewer emissions from the burning of fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas. That's been shown in scenarios modeled by researchers with the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, or IPCC.

Thanks to renewable energy and green technologies, those scenarios have already become reality in several countries and regions.

Recent findings suggest that the economies of developed countries like the United Kingdom, the United States, Japanand Australia have experienced years of growth alongside sinking CO2 emissions. That's even when offshore production is included.

In the European Union, the bloc-wide economy has grown by more than 70% since 1990. Meanwhile, the EU's carbon emissions have dropped by around 40%.

But such a complete decoupling of growth and emissions is, according to Haberl and his fellow researchers, relatively rare.

In India, and in several countries in Africa and Southeast Asia, economies are becoming more efficient. But while economic performance is outpacing emissions growth, emissions are still rising in those countries and globally. This is not compatible with preventing the worst impacts of climate change.

"That doesn't mean, however, that it couldn't work in the future," remarked Haberl, referring to decoupling of growth and emissions.

And even though economic growth has been shown to be compatible with emissions reduction, eliminating all greenhouse gases from a polluting industry like steel or chemicals is complicated.

These sectors don't just release emissions by burning fossil fuels for energy; carbon is also a key part of the chemical processes used to create their products, notably in the steel industry.

Replacing it with greener substitutes, or an alternative energy source like green hydrogen, requires significant investment.

There's another hurdle: the world's high consumption of resources. A productive economy depends on many raw materials and other products: ores, chemicals, wood, cement, glass and agricultural products.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Many countries are now using green technologies to reduce the amount of resources needed to manufacture a product, for example, and are making their economies more efficient.

It has been revealed that but that doesn't mean overall fewer resources are being used because falling costs can encourage businesses to produce more things and people to consume more. This can partially offset green savings and is called the rebound effect.

The British economy has been growing for years, emissions have been dropping and efficiency has increased, but the UK still used 7% more resources in 2023 than it did in 2001.

Sources indicate that global resource consumption has tripled over the last 50 years. If the world continues on the current pathway, that could increase by another 60% by 2060. It remains unclear whether green growth can deliver the emissions and resource reductions needed to stop climate change and biodiversity loss rapidly enough.

"We really need to move beyond efficiency gains in our existing production practices to look more broadly at what we consume," said Catherine Ganzleben, a sustainability and fair transitions expert at the European Environment Agency.

She told DW that people also need to reconsider how they consume and whether they really need to own everything they use in their daily life — cars, for example.

"But we can shift towards models where we share cars, so we pool our resources and have significantly lower resources per person through sharing the goods that we need.".

Some researchers have concluded that unrestricted economic growth is no longer possible in the long term, even if it's sustainable.

In a recent development, instead, they've called for degrowth. This posits slower economic growth, no growth at all or even negative growth, so that the world's ecosystems and the climate have a chance to recover and stabilize.

That applies mainly to economies in richer countries, which would need to take targeted steps to reduce their energy and resource use. Poorer countries would continue to grow until their economies and quality of life improve significantly.

Sources indicate that under the degrowth theory, a society's prosperity is not measured solely by the growth of its gross domestic product, but by values such as quality of life, education and community. The idea is that once countries develop to a certain point, additional growth doesn't translate into greater well-being.

In a recent development, ultimately, the concept is based on the idea that human well-being and ecological sustainability is only possible in the long term with a planned, socially just reduction of material production and resource consumption. Degrowth advocates argue this would be preferable to an unplanned and potentially catastrophic economic contraction caused by escalating climate extremes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A 2020 study by researchers from the universities of Leeds and Lausanne demonstrated that the concept of degrowth supported the world's climate goals — and that a high quality of life didn't have to be sacrificed in exchange for a significantly lower consumption of energy and resources.

However, there is still no conclusive evidence that an entire modern economy could continue to function entirely on the degrowth principles in the long term.

Nevertheless, Haberl doesn't assume that an environmentally friendly economic model automatically goes hand in hand with sacrifice, arguing instead for a needs-based economy.

Industry observers note that "A society isn't necessarily better off when it's producing more goods and services," he said. It all depends on how prosperity and quality of life are measured in the future, and how states decide to do business.

It has been revealed that today, a successful economy is measured by the growth of a country's gross domestic product — put simply, the worth of all of its goods and services. This calculation doesn't account for income distribution, unpaid work, quality of life or environmental damage.

In a recent development, "The highest possible real incomes for every individual would probably not be compatible with ecological goals in the long term," stated Haberl. "On the other hand, an increase in prosperity — related to a higher quality of life — would be.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that an analysis by the European Environment Agency (EEA) pointed out that the idea of steady growth is part of the world's economic cycle, and deeply anchored in our institutions, norms and societal discourse. The job market and tax system are also closely tied to gross domestic product growth. A shrinking economy would therefore require a fundamental shift in our way of thinking.

Countries face a dilemma: a steadily growing economy is not compatible with ecological goals, according to the EEA. On the other side, a sharp decline in growth could trigger enormous social upheaval.

Recent findings suggest that and the correlation is much more complex than the idea of "less is more," as highlighted by an EEA study in November 2021. "The fact that GDP growth has been harmful for the environment does not necessarily mean that declining GDP would be good for the environment," noted the report.

Achieving green growth while respecting environmental limits would require an "unprecedented decoupling of economic activity from environmental and climate pressures. Whether this is feasible is right now uncertain.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the third straight time, the Washington Spirit are playing for the NWSL Championship.
  • In a recent development, the Washington Spirit won it all in 2021 but came up just short in each of the last two finals.
  • The Kansas City Current bring plenty to the final and may just be the favorites.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the third straight time, the Washington Spirit are playing for the NWSL Championship. The No. 3 Spirit host the No. 4 Kansas City Current at Audi Field on Saturday for the biggest prize in domestic women's soccer. Kickoff is at 8 p.m. ET, and you can see it all on CBS and Paramount+.

In a recent development, the Washington Spirit won it all in 2021 but came up just short in each of the last two finals. This may be the day that Trinity Rodman gets her second crown.

The Kansas City Current bring plenty to the final and may just be the favorites. They're back in the significant game for the first time since 2022 after ending NJ/NY Gotham FC's title defense in the semis. Croix Bethune, who used to play for the Spirit, curled in a free-kick stunner, and Haley Hopkins won it in the 89th minute.

So who lifts the trophy? Our experts make their picks below.

Industry observers note that star-studded attack: This year's finalists did not have the most straightforward journeys to the NWSL Championship, but the good news for each of them is that there will be few excuses when they finally take to the pitch on Saturday. Trinity Rodman is about to cap off a career-best campaign after an injury-riddled 2025 season and will be joined by the impactful Sofia Cantore and midseason arrival Clara Luvanga, putting the Washington Spirit in as good a position as any to come out with a win that has eluded them over the last two seasons. The Current, though, are in the same boat --  they have struggled without their all-star trio, but each of Croix Bethune, Temwa Chawinga and Michelle Cooper will be available on Saturday and equally capable of turning the game in their favor.

According to recent reports, midfield battles: There's going to be a real display of veteran prowess and eager energy. Both teams have experienced players and rising stars, and it'll be a combo of chess and tug of war during the NWSL Championship. Washington Spirit's Andi Sullivan anchors most things in the middle, with Leicy Santos linking play and Melissa Bethi's recent rise in form. Even with all the changes from injuries to departures and returns from maternity leave, the Spirit are gelling at a good time in a crucial part of the pitch. They'll battle against Kansas City's Lo'eau LaBonta and Vanessa DiBernardo, two of the best in the league with longevity and finesse. Ball knowers understand that they're two players who can control a game, close and create lanes, or serve up goals and assists. Add attacking mid Croix Bethune into the mix, and Kansas City have plenty of ways to win the middle of the park. -- Sandra Herrera.

Balance: At their best, the Washington Spirit are a side who can win a game in multiple ways, and while there's plenty of star power on both sides, balance is where they win out. It's a fascinating match for both sides and one where the margins will be thin but being able to have a strong attack led by Trinity Rodman along with a buildup that Andi Sullivan keeps control of. If the Spirit can control the pace, it will be a long day for Kansas City but Croix Bethune will have ideas of her own as well. -- Chuck Booth.

Industry observers note that washington Spirit: The Spirit have tossed around the phrase that the third time's the charm after two empty-handed trips to the NWSL Championship and this year, it's hard not to buy the argument. Rodman is happy and healthy but she is just one part of a team that has been smartly assembled over the years and seems as cohesive as ever. -- Pardeep Cattry.

In a recent development, washington Spirit: Truthfully, the pressure is on the Washington Spirit headed into this one, and that typically doesn't play out the best for teams who are the higher seed or considered favorites on paper. Kansas City will be a more than worthy opponent, but the Spirit's third time in the final comes with a long home build-up through and back to Audi Field, and any mental component needed will come with a boost from the crowd environment. -- Sandra Herrera.

According to recent reports, washington Spirit: Sure, this is a "neutral" venue, but being a home team in a final match will carry the Spirit at Rowdy Audi. Considering that this is the third consecutive final, fans snatched up tickets as soon as they could, assuming that the home side would be here. While all the pressure is on the Spirit and rightfully so, the team has also embraced that, and once the first goal goes in the net, this is going to turn into a party. -- Chuck Booth.

Industry observers note that trinity Rodman: Is this an obvious choice? Yes, yes it is, but to be fair, Rodman has earned the right to be the easy pick. She has always been key to the Spirit's success but hit a latest level this season, to the point that she had a very valid MVP case even if her ex-teammate Ashley Sanchez took it home instead after a record-breaking season with the North Carolina Courage. Rodman's ability to create and score chances means she's very likely to have a say on Saturday, one that could very well end the Spirit's five-year wait for another championship. -- Pardeep Cattry.

In a recent development, clara Luvanga: The last few NWSL Championship MVPs have gone to the lone goal scorer. Barbra Banda won it in 2024 for her game-winning goal, and Rose Lavelle earned it for her single title goal in 2025. If these two teams match up on the pitch as evenly as they do on paper, then it could come down to a single moment again, and Luvanga has shown she's better positioned for it with her current form. Her four goals and three assists through seven games make her an efficient threat on goal, and could finally be the difference maker for the group in their third final. -- Sandra Herrera.

Trinity Rodman: To win finals, you need your best players to be at their best. All eyes have been on Trinity Rodman this season after she became the highest-paid player in NWSL history, and she has delivered. Considering that the next development in her career is to become a player for the biggest moments, and capping off the final by scoring will be just the way to do it. -- Chuck Booth.

The untold story of Mauricio Pochettino's move to Man United: When club decided he was the right man, the moment it became 'real', emotional talks with US staff and whirlwind first days in charge

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1729 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:25 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the fresh head coach of Manchester United.
  • The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:25 EST, 22 November 2026.

When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the fresh head coach of Manchester United.

The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.

Industry observers note that however, United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25 left Carrick’s job hanging by a thread. He was given a two-week stay of execution that also allowed United time to step up their search for a suitable replacement.

At a meeting of the club’s executive committee on November 5 – after United had lost to Chelsea and staged a chaotic Champions League win against Roma – it was decided that Pochettino would be the No.1 choice if Carrick was sacked.

By the time the Argentine caught that flight to Atlanta 24 hours later to take charge of the USA's two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, United were preparing to make their move.

This is the story of the whirlwind two weeks that will end with Pochettino taking charge of his first game as United boss against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday following the dramatic events on both sides of the Atlantic.

In a recent development, patrick Dorgu’s injury-time header rescued United from another defeat as they snatched a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, but it wasn’t enough to save Carrick. His fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp.

There is a five-hour time difference between Manchester and Georgia, so it was late afternoon when Pochettino first learned of United’s interest at the Trilith Guesthouse – close to the US national team’s training base in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta – as the players began to report there for duty.

Michael Carrick's fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

As speculation raged over Carrick’s future, the odds on Pochettino replacing him at Old Trafford were slashed after some massive money was placed on the 54-year-old overnight.

Preliminary talks continued with his representatives who made the US Soccer Federation aware of the situation. Pochettino discussed it over dinner at the team hotel with chief executive JT Batson and chief operating officer Dan Helfrich who knew it was pointless trying to change his mind.

According to recent reports, ‘That was the major day,’ states a source close to Pochettino, who took US team training in Fayetteville. ‘It became real and the optimism grew.’.

As talks accelerated between United and their prospective newly introduced head coach, Carrick returned to Carrington to work with the United players not on international duty while chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and rubber-stamp the change.

United reached verbal agreement with Pochettino over a two-and-a-half-year deal, and agreed to pay US Soccer around £10million to buy the 54-year-old and his staff – No 2 Jesus Perez, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino (Mauricio’s son), strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott – out of their contracts.

In a recent development, there was never any question of him leaving before the two Haiti ties, even though it left little time before his first game against Liverpool. Pochettino is stated to have been respectful of the USA’s position and felt an obligation to see the job through.

As a compromise, it was agreed that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr would be allowed to leave for Manchester after the first leg regardless of the result.

Media in the US were informed that access to the players had been cancelled out of respect for Veterans Day. It also meant that they don’t have to answer questions about Pochettino’s future.

Carrick returned to Carrington at 7.50am for the last time as United head coach and was sacked in a meeting with Berrada and Wilcox.

By the time Pochettino woke up in Fayetteville, United officially had a managerial vacancy and he gathered the players together for a scheduled team briefing at 10am.

Pochettino went through the usual pre-match preparation, and then invited staff into the room for the second half of the meeting.

It has been revealed that there was some emotion but no surprise when he informed them of his decision to take the United job. ‘As you’d expect, he spoke from the heart,’ notes a source. ‘He loved being here but United was a dream opportunity. It was too hard to say no, but hard to say goodbye.’.

United officially declared Pochettino’s appointment and confirmed that he would stay in charge for the USA’s two games against Haiti before starting work the following Wednesday.

Pochettino conducted his pre-match press conference in Fayetteville, flanked by CEO chief JT Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, and broke down in tears as he thanked them for their support over the last 26 months.

Otherwise, the preparation is remarked to have gone according to proposal as the US squad flew to Miami.

The Argentine broke down in tears as he thanked the USA for their support over the last 26 months.

The US smashed Haiti 6-0 to all but guarantee their place in the semi-finals. Even so the message from Pochettino to his players after the game was: ‘This tie isn’t over.’.

The players learned for the first time that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr were leaving camp, and they headed straight to Manchester.

Pochettino flew with the players from Miami to Cincinnati for the second leg at the TQL Stadium.

On a visit to the Kenwood Towne Centre shopping mall, a man whose profile had risen in the US during his two years in charge of the national team was approached by even more fans than normal.

When Pochettino appeared as a guest of honour at the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium that night, a number of Bengals’ players and staff congratulated him on his upcoming job claiming to be United fans.

It emerged that United had provided a private jet for Pochettino and the remainder of his staff to fly straight from Cincinnati to Manchester through the night after the second leg.

In his pre-match press conference, he confirmed the departure of his three coaches over the weekend, and it was no surprise to learn that he was in constant contact over several days as he prepared to join them at Carrington.

According to recent reports, the US beat Haiti by two goals to complete an 8-0 aggregate win. Afterwards, they played Take Me Home, Country Roads by John Denver over the stadium PA, which has been a tradition since the US hosted the World Cup last summer but carried particular poignance given that it has also been adopted as an anthem at United.

Pochettino invited all the staff onto the pitch for a team photo as he led a chant of U-S-A, and there was a tearful send-off in the dressing-room as he was presented with a signed shirt and a special hand-painted bottle of Clase Azul tequila.

It’s a favourite tipple of Pochettino’s and staff also ordered food from Chick-fil-A, which Pochettino regrets won’t be available in Manchester.

He never had a permanent residence in America, so he left the stadium at 10.30pm with the same suitcase he had brought from London and headed for Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport for the flight to Manchester.

Pochettino had a poor night’s sleep before landing shortly before noon aboard the grey Gulfstream G700 jet with D’Agostino, Scott and Tuya.

He posted a picture from the skies above Manchester and was then driven to Carrington, changing into an official United tracksuit en route.

Pochettino was too late for training but met with some of the players and club executives before being given a tour of the training ground and conducting an interview with MUTV which wrapped up about 7pm. He stayed at the training ground long into the evening to catch up on his preparation for Liverpool.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United.

It has been revealed that more players returned from international duty, but Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online. It was proof – if he needed it – that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will be under even greater scrutiny at United.

According to recent reports, responding, Pochettino said: 'We have young guys training with us. It’s not nice. It’s not good.

'What do they want to show? Yes, we were working on shape. We were very organised. What is the point of doing something that can be very dangerous?

'I don't want to be upset, but I think it's a process the club is caring a lot about.'.

Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online.

Having only trained for a couple of hours on Thursday, Pochettino worked with the players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

‘The training session was a little bit longer than it normally is in (match day) minus two,’ said Pochettino at his opening pre-match press conference, admitting that he had not even had a chance to shower beforehand.

Pochettino worked with his fresh players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

Pochettino took training for the third day running at Carrington on Saturday morning, before United travelled on the team bus to their hotel where they had dinner and a pre-match meeting last night.

On Sunday he faces a massive first game as United boss in front of the cameras at Anfield at the end of a dizzying fortnight.

  • In a recent development, "Harry Kane underwent successful surgery overnight after tearing his left ankle ligament in yesterday's home match against 1.
  • Counting down the days already ❤️‍🩹 pic.twitter.com/rpNWUxc4vW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich's depth was already pushed to the limit, but Friday's 1-1 draw with Koln may have broken Vincent Kompany's side. Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane lasted only 20 minutes before exiting with what the club is calling a "syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle," which required surgery overnight and will keep him sidelined "for months," according to sporting director Max Eberl.

In a recent development, "Harry Kane underwent successful surgery overnight after tearing his left ankle ligament in yesterday's home match against 1. FC Köln. The 33-year-old will now begin his rehab," Bayern remarked in a statement.

Counting down the days already ❤️‍🩹 pic.twitter.com/rpNWUxc4vW.

Losing Kane alone is a significant blow to the Bavarians after they failed to replace Nicolas Jackson when his loan ended, but the injuries didn't stop there. Michael Olise was also withdrawn at halftime and left the stadium on crutches.

Industry observers note that this led to a match in which Bayern put only one shot on target against a side just above the relegation zone, showing this is a problem of their own creation in the transfer market. Coming into the season without a viable backup for an aging Kane would eventually hurt Bayern, and Kompany now needs to oversee a worst-case scenario. Luis Diaz and Ismael Saibari were already out with injuries, and when Kane went down, Thomas Bischof had to come in for him instead of a like-for-like striker. Even with Jamal Musiala's neurological challenges, the players they do have aren't able to perform at their best.

Recent findings suggest that already in an actual title race in the Bundesliga with Borussia Dortmund, these are the kinds of setbacks that can lead to a latest German champion for the first time since Bayer Leverkusen in 2023-24, and even they had to go undefeated to accomplish that feat, while this season could be Bayern's own undoing. They've been one of the top sides in the world when healthy, but as it is, this side will struggle in Champions League play, where they'll travel to face Lille. Precariously in 13th place in the Champions League league phase, Bayern won't fall out of the top 24 without Kane, but it could get close to something that they should be concerned about. Even missing out on the top eight and needing to play additional games is something that Bayern won't want to deal with, considering this injury crisis.

Recent findings suggest that being a backup to Kane is a thankless task, as it's hard to get game time and you're also compared to one of the best players in the world, but it's still a multifaceted failure for Bayern to not have one. Real Madrid were able to recruit post-prime players to back up Karim Benzema, and now Kylian Mbappe has a backup from the academy. There's no reason that a club of Bayern's stature shouldn't be able to do the same, but here we are in the same position they constantly find themselves in.

It has been revealed that depth issues have held Bayern back from claiming a Champions League title in recent years. Kane winning the Ballon d'Or solidified that the starting XI is more than good enough to lift Europe's most coveted club trophy, and the difference between this side and the 2020 one that won the Champions League is their lack of depth.

It's a strange situation with Musiala that isn't being handled well, with board members open to selling him, and it doesn't help the club's overall trajectory. Bayern will need to shake things up in January, but these concerns began long before now, and to return to the top of the global game, they need to change the way they do things.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Borussia Dortmundâs brand-fresh away kit for the 2025/26 season has sparked fury among supporters, prompting the club to acknowledge the backlash and vow to respond.

The kit, which combines a white base with black sleeves and neon yellow detailing, was worn for the first time in Saturdayâs 2-0 Bundesliga win over Heidenheim.

But instead of excitement, its debut was met with anger in the stands and online. Fans unfurled banners blasting it as âthe cruelest jersey in the leagueâ while chants of âWe want black and yellow jerseysâ rang out before kick-off, a pointed reminder of the clubâs traditional colours.

Industry observers note that across social media, the reaction was no kinder. Many supporters branded the design a betrayal of Dortmundâs historic identity, with critics arguing it looks more like a training top than a shirt fit for the famous Schwarzgelben.

Club bosses have now pledged to listen.

Industry observers note that managing director Carsten Cramer took personal responsibility for the fallout, telling reporters: "The criticism has been received, and we are addressing it. The responsibility lies with me. We won't always be able to please everyone when selecting jerseys.".

Sporting director Sebastian Kehl was more measured, reminding fans that opinions on kit design are always split.

Recent findings suggest that "I think we have different opinions about jerseys every year," he mentioned. "It will never be the case that a Borussia Dortmund jersey meets with 100 percent approval. Fundamentally, we know which colors represent our city and our club, and that this is reflected in the design of almost all jerseys.".

It has been revealed that he added, with a touch of humour: "However, there are also people who want something younger, something fresh, something creative. The fresh jersey brought BVB three points in Heidenheim. A successful jersey, I'd say. Everything else is a discussion that we as a club consider normal.".

Whether the kit makes another appearance when Dortmund travel to Mainz on September 27 remains to be seen, but if it does, you best believe that Dortmund fans to have something to say about it.

Dangerous words perhaps when you work for Evangelos Marinakis, but John Percy reported this week that Glasner was backed by his players in a squad meeting.

Glasner has happy memories of playing City, beating them in the 2025 FA Cup final with Crystal Palace, but his Forest reign is in urgent need of a signature victory and performance.

Leeds expose Chelsea's unresolved defensive problems as Xabi Alonso's crew yet to find footing

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1130 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that LONDON -- This was supposed to be the year, the time when Chelsea grew up and a proper manager started extracting consistent performances from a squad whose much-vaunted talent is too rarely expressed in results form.
  • Once more, however, that is threatening to be a standard beyond Chelsea.
  • Right backs in midfield, center backs as nominal left wing backs that are actually auxiliary central midfielders, switching the right wing back to center forward: in isolation, you could make a case for so many of these adjustments.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that LONDON -- This was supposed to be the year, the time when Chelsea grew up and a proper manager started extracting consistent performances from a squad whose much-vaunted talent is too rarely expressed in results form. In this most in-flux of Premier League seasons, Xabi Alonso still might leave her with something. It is not going to take particular excellence for a club like this to achieve the bare minimum of Champions League qualification. Adequacy might do it.

Once more, however, that is threatening to be a standard beyond Chelsea. This 4-1 defeat at home to old rivals Leeds has them squeezed into the Premier League's middle ground, those above them very visible proof of how much more can be done with less. There is nothing false about that position. Since the last weeks of summer, Alonso's team have given up so much at the back that their likeliest route to success seemed to be supernova seasons from all three of Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro. Nothing else would paper over the cracks in the defense.

And Alonso has tried a lot. Right backs in midfield, center backs as nominal left wing backs that are actually auxiliary central midfielders, switching the right wing back to center forward: in isolation, you could make a case for so many of these adjustments. When the performances are so inconsistent, why not change the XI every game? Alonso's success at Bayer Leverkusen, coupled with the inquisitive footballing mind that made the player so beloved of elite coaches, have earned him the right to experiment.

Every change, however, begs the question of what the foundations underlying all this are. Those ought to have shone through this afternoon. Alonso's was as straightforward an XI as he has named. Estevao, Palmer and Rogers off an orthodox center forward, Moises Caicedo running the double pivot and an orthodox back four in front of Emiliano Martinez. This looked like a team intent on playing its way.

Instead, they had Leeds' game foisted upon them. That might have been different if they had not lost Caicedo. He seemed to have a handle on the game before colliding with James Justin as both competed for a high ball. Those often seemed like the only sort up for grabs today; even when Chelsea played well, they were playing the sort of game Leeds wanted. This wasn't quite the rapid attacking up the gut with which Xabi Alonso charmed the Premier League early in this season. It was bypass the press-ball, get it straight up to the final third and see what comes of it.

Industry observers note that it can work. Justin, exemplary as a man-marker without the ball and roving agent of chaos in the Chelsea half, cleared a goal kick straight into the back of Morgan Rogers. He moved swiftly up the Leeds gut, his pass to Emmanuel Emegha delivered at just the right moment for the Premier League debutant to slam in the opener. It was perhaps the only moment of clinical execution from the Blues.

Sources indicate that they needed so many more. After all, this is a team that fails to meet the standards in so many aspects of defending. They press like a newly promoted team. They always seem to name one defender who can be picked on in the duels (starting left back Pep Charravia ranks 101st of 102 defenders for duel success over 300-plus Premier League minutes). Midfielders routinely abandon runners. When Caicedo left this game the feint thread holding the team together was cut.

No one had the composure to deal with the bouncing ball moments after Emegha's opener, Noah Okafor free to move into the box and shoot low through a crowd of legs. No one seemed truly live to the danger for Okafor's second, thundered into the roof of the net when Chelsea could not repel pressure down their right. Between that a contentious penalty, Jayden Bogle's long-range effort striking Rogers right in the grey area between sleeve and arm. If that hadn't been the moment when Chelsea caved, another would have come along.

Recent findings suggest that "Leeds believed more than us," Alonso admitted. "We didn't show a good enough reaction." The quick one-two punch had been more than enough to send Chelsea heads to the floor.

A two-goal deficit ought not to be beyond their reach, but the final 32 minutes saw them outshot seven to six with fewer passes completed into the penalty area. Palmer's most notable action of this game was to row with Joao Pedro as he made his way down the tunnel. Nothing he could have done would have overcome the problems Chelsea made for themselves at the other end. It really wouldn't hurt, though if he did more than nothing.

These feel like problems unresolved by a manager who was supposed to be the savior. Eleven Premier League games is not a lot to turn the tide but it is enough to give us a sense of who this team are. The answer is a team whose early scoring streak covered for a below-average attack (1.25 non-penalty expected goals per game, 14th in the Premier League) and a below-average defense (1.44 non-penalty expected goals allowed per game, 15th in the Premier League). The game state-warping impact of scoring with your first shot can only mitigate so much.

Is it time for a conversation about Alonso and pressure? If so it has to be caveated by the unity and purpose he fostered at Bayer Leverkusen, qualities this dressing room sorely needs. He might not have corralled the superstars at Real Madrid but the press and possession system he forged could have achieved great things given time. Stitching together a version of this Chelsea, overloaded with number 10s and underpowered defensive players, that suits the more direct and chaotic Premier League was always going to be a coaching challenge.

Industry observers note that and of course this is not the Roman Abramovich era. Swapping out coaches is not a silver bullet for perennial trophy contenders but instead the modus operandi of an ownership group that are the most serious problem at Stamford Bridge. Someone is going to have to be afforded time to corral this squad or indeed tear it down and start again. Doing that is going to be a club-wide effort, including fans. Few of them hung around to wave off a side who had allowed old rivals Leeds a first win at Stamford Bridge since 1999, the same side who had let Tottenham break the habit of a lifetime last month.

In a recent development, the vibes are bad. The performances might be worse. This brand new start is feeling all too familiar.

Once again, Berlin is rolling out the red carpet, and once again the focus is on Ukraine: Around 20 heads of state and government, primarily from across Europe, are set to gather in the German capital on Thursday (November 19). They will discuss the future of the Eastern European country that has been under attack from Russia since February 2022 and is now facing yet another harsh winter.

In a recent development, extensive security measures have already been announced for Berlin's government district, pointing to the presence of high-ranking participants. It remains unclear whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will be among them. What does appear certain, however, is the attendance of chief US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, according to several media outlets.

According to recent reports, the "Coalition of the Willing" is a group of 36 countries determined not to be deterred from supporting the nation under attack. Unlike other international forums, the group is focused not only on how to support Ukraine militarily and financially in the here and now.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Led by Germany, France and the United Kingdom, the coalition is also prepared, in principle, to help monitor a possible ceasefire within Ukraine itself and to contribute to the complex security guarantees the country would then require, should such a scenario come to pass. The effort dates back to March 2025, when the countries involved first met in London.

But what can the coalition realistically achieve? Stefan Meister of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) is not overly optimistic.

Recent findings suggest that "The fundamental problem is that Europe has yet to put forward a proposal," he told DW. "There is no initiative outlining what security guarantees Europe would offer, what troops it would be prepared to deploy, what measures it could provide to safeguard a ceasefire, or where it would be willing to make compromises.".

It has been revealed that nevertheless, the meeting comes at a moment when some observers believe there may finally be movement toward ending the war. During talks in Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates a few days ago, Russia, Ukraine and the US managed to agree only on a prisoner exchange. It was a modest step forward.

Further talks are planned, and it has been a long time since the prospects appeared as favorable as they do now for Europe to secure a role in future decisions on war and peace in Ukraine.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has repeatedly been argued, both by US officials and by those in power in Russia, that Europe does not speak with a single voice.

This has sparked a debate among EU heads of state and government over who, exactly, could represent Europe in such talks. Could it be German Chancellor Friedrich Merz of the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU)?

After the EU summit in Dublin, Ireland, on Friday, Merz said: "For the first time, concrete peace talks are expected to take place in the coming weeks with Europe represented. Germany has a seat at the table, that is absolutely clear.".

But what exactly did that mean? That Germany alone would speak for all of Europe? Hardly. As was also made clear in Berlin on Monday, Europe would be represented by the E3 countries, namely Germany, France, and the non-EU member United Kingdom, joined by Poland and Italy. Official EU representatives, including European Council President Antonio Costa, would also take part.

Stefan Meister of the DGAP believes the debate claims a great deal about the pressures Europe itself is under.

According to recent reports, "Europe's positioning has more to do with domestic political considerations than with developments in the negotiations," Meister stated. "Everyone needs to show that they are participating in the talks in some way. Elections will be held next year in France and Poland, and it is still unclear whether French support for Ukraine will continue in its current form after that.".

German Deputy Government Spokesperson Sebastian Hille, meanwhile, sought to downplay the debate on Monday over a possible role for Friedrich Merz as chief negotiator.

At the federal government's regular press briefing, he said: "This is not about discussing individuals. What matters is that Putin finally understands that he must come to the negotiating table so that we have a chance of achieving peace in the first place.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US negotiator Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, struck a rather different tone last week.

Speaking in Abu Dhabi, he stated: "If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiations.".

Government spokesperson Hille responded on Monday: "Europe's strength lies precisely in the unity and cohesion of many countries. We should not allow ourselves to be drawn into debates that others want to frame around this question.".

According to recent reports, hille emphasized that the situation remained unchanged: Peace in Ukraine could only be achieved step by step. Europe, too, would need stamina, perseverance and a willingness to undertake the painstaking work required to bring it about.

It has been revealed that european supporters of Ukraine are also under pressure as public opinion on the problem is shifting, including in Germany. While a broad majority favored helping defend the country in the immediate aftermath of Russia's invasion in the spring of 2022, support has since fallen markedly.

According to the latest DeutschlandTrend survey on the issue, conducted or German public broadcaster ARD in September 2026, 52% of eligible voters still support weapons deliveries to Ukraine, while 42% believe such support has gone too far. That is the highest level of opposition recorded since the start of the war.

Sources indicate that A further study conducted for public broadcaster WDR in November 2026 found that support for Ukraine has become a more polarizing glitch in Germany than immigration. According to the survey, 54% of respondents favor continued support for Ukraine, while just under 29% would prefer a rapprochement with Russia, despite its war of aggression against Ukraine.

#105669. The world has a golden chance to improve HIV prevention: don’t squander it

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1309 w)

The world has a golden chance to improve HIV prevention: don’t squander it

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1309 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • South Africa’s health officials at the launch in June of lenacapavir, a drug that provides strong protection against HIV when administered twice a year.Credit: Per-Anders Pettersson/Getty.
  • Earlier this month, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a generic version of the HIV drug lenacapavir for use as a preventive treatment.
  • A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

South Africa’s health officials at the launch in June of lenacapavir, a drug that provides strong protection against HIV when administered twice a year.Credit: Per-Anders Pettersson/Getty.

Earlier this month, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a generic version of the HIV drug lenacapavir for use as a preventive treatment. Twice-yearly injections of this game-changing medicine — originally developed by the tech giant Gilead Sciences in Foster City, California — have been shown to be more than 95% effective at preventing HIV acquisition1. At the same time, as Nature reports in a News feature, an HIV vaccine — that would ultimately be a more robust solution to preventing HIV — is closer than ever before.

A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies.

A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies.

Recent findings suggest that in 2024, Gilead signed licensing agreements with six pharmaceutical companies, allowing them to make and sell generic versions of lenacapavir in 120 low- and middle-income countries, subject to regulatory approval. The recent FDA approval brings access a step closer in these countries. The cost to owners has been set at US$40 per year, fuelling hopes that the drug will help to bring the global HIV epidemic under control.

These welcome developments contrast with the situation of public funding for HIV research and treatment, which is reeling from deep and unconscionable cuts from the US government. Many of the researchers whom Nature spoke to for the News feature had been funded by a programme for preclinical HIV-vaccine research run by the US National Institutes of Health (NIH). But the agency ended the programme last year, forcing researchers to scale back their research and seek alternative funding. Whatever funding comes next is likely to be less stable and less predictable than the NIH funding. It’s imperative that the cuts be reversed — or upcoming government funding sources found.

The path to an HIV vaccine has been long and bumpy, with decades of high-profile and costly failures, but there is now light at the end of the tunnel. The latest strategy — known as germline targeting — is designed to trigger the production of rare, highly potent antibodies that can prevent infection with diverse HIV strains. The technique has shown encouraging results in animal models2–4 and in early trials in humans5. Researchers are more optimistic than they’ve been in years that an effective HIV vaccine could be on the horizon.

The end of AIDS is in sight: don’t abandon PEPFAR now.

The end of AIDS is in sight: don’t abandon PEPFAR now.

It has been revealed that but in the meantime, antiretroviral drugs such as lenacapavir look poised to have a big impact on infection prevention. In Africa alone, upcoming infections could be cut by around one-third if just 5% of adults most likely to acquire HIV received the drug, and by half if it was given to one-fifth of adults, according to the Gates Foundation’s Institute for Disease Modelling in Seattle, Washington.

It has been revealed that but lenacapavir alone is unlikely to bring the HIV epidemic fully under control. There are several reasons for this: first, it’s not always easy to determine who needs the drug most. Second, to be effective, the drug must be taken for most of someone’s life — or at least while they are sexually active. Third, even $40 a year is unaffordable for people on the very lowest incomes.

Until recently, the United States was the stand-out funder for antiretroviral drugs for people living with HIV in low-and middle-income countries. That stopped in January 2025, when the US administration suspended funding. Although it later restored a limited amount, the effects have been devastating. A survey published earlier this year found that some 1,700 facilities previously offering treatments to people living with HIV had closed as a result (see go.nature.com/4a7ftp4).

In a recent development, trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

Trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

Such instability highlights the importance of vaccines. “The funding cuts that happened in the past couple of years have really made it even more obvious how fragile that system of reliance” on drug access is, says Penny Moore, a virologist at South Africa’s National Institute for Communicable Disease in Johannesburg. And that fragility, as Rogier Sanders, an HIV-vaccine researcher at Amsterdam University Medical Centre, says, is why research into a vaccine remains a priority: “A vaccine makes you independent from access to drugs.”.

But the US cuts have not only curtailed the preclinical vaccine programme, they have also forced the postponement and scaling back of an HIV vaccine trial in South Africa. They have also affected supporting research, such as surveillance efforts tracking HIV evolution in African countries, states Nairobi-based Vincent Muturi-Kioi, who is leading development of HIV vaccines at the International AIDS Vaccine Initiative in New York City.

Success stories such as the repurposing of lenacapavir as a preventive treatment and progress in vaccine development show the importance of investment in health. It is imperative that HIV vaccine research and deployment continues to receive support, at the same time as rolling out lenacapavir as widely as possible.

It could take more than a decade to translate the encouraging results with germline targeting into an effective HIV vaccine, and the current strategy might encounter more hurdles.

In a recent development, the world is closer than it has ever been to an effective HIV vaccine and has a drug capable of preventing infections. Now is the time for funders to ramp up investment, not cut it back.

Jayden Bogle on what it’s like to be backed by the Leeds United faithful

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to English football’s best atmospheres, few can match the noise and fury of a packed Elland Road.

Since joining Leeds United from Yorkshire rivals Sheffield United in 2024, Jayden Bogle has been able to experience this on a regular basis, with his defensive efforts and lung-busting runs forward bringing the cheers of the Elland Road faithful week-in, week-out.

This backing helped Bogle’s side win promotion back to the Premier League in the right-back’s first season in West Yorkshire, which was followed up by a respectable 14th-place finish back in the top flight last term.

Leeds’ return to the Premier League last season came against Everton, a match which left a lasting impression on Bogle.

“The first game of last season [a 1-0 win over Everton] was top, that atmosphere,” he tells FourFourTwo.

“You really feel the impact of what the fans and the stadium can do, especially when we're making chances or someone puts in a big tackle or block. You can feel the energy instantly from the fans.”.

The Leeds fanbase has taken its fair share of knocks over the years, and while Bogle knows just how key building this authentic connection with the fans is, it has to be done in the right way.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

“As players, you work all year round to stay as professional as you can,” he continues. “You try to have that relationship with the fans, but you've got to stay professional at the same time.”.

Leeds’ promotion campaign, which saw them win the Championship title with virtually the last kick of the season, sparked huge celebrations in the city, climaxing in an estimated 150,000 fans lining the streets for an open top bus parade.

For Bogle, this was finally a chance to share in the moment with the club’s supporters.

"On that day, it was nice to be able to really bond with them, especially after the parade.

“Everyone was on the same page, happy and enjoying it. When we got on the bus and headed towards the city centre, it was something I'd never seen before – flares going off, people everywhere.

“It's a day that I'll never forget.”.

For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown.
